title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: The tape tells you what institutions are actually doing with their money, even when the valuation makes value investors uncomfortable.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Adaptation

web_blocks.html: While valuation flashes caution at 107x trailing P/E, the price tape on NSE:SEDEMAC shows a mixed-but-constructive weekly base. At the November 13, 2026 close of ₹3,129.10 (+0.42% 1D, +2.67% 1W, -1.15% 1M, +56.44% 6M), `stage2_evaluation` tags SEDEMAC in Stage 2 based on weekly averages [22]. However, because it has only 167 daily bars since its March 11, 2026 listing, the `market_facts` ledger marks daily stage as N/A (insufficient history) with a flat-to-falling 50-DMA (₹3,138.55 vs ₹3,144.84 ten days prior). Weekly structure anchors the trend: price sits +13.46% above its rising 30-week SMA (₹2,757.91) and right on its 10-week EMA (₹3,116.67, +0.40%) [22].

web_blocks.html: Our multi-timeframe scan (`options_snapshot.py`) identifies a STAGE2_VCP_VOLATILITY_SQUEEZE [22]. Bollinger bandwidth has narrowed to 7.2%, and November 13 volume was just 63,021 shares (0.49x the 30-day average of 129,314) [22]. The 63-day volume dry-up ratio sits at 0.19. On the 4-hour chart, EMA20 (₹3,111.64) and SMA50 (₹3,140.04) have converged with 4H RSI at 51.33. Meanwhile, FIIs raised their stake from 2.52% in March 2026 to 10.30% in September 2026 [1, 20]. DIIs trimmed from 43.93% to 38.34%, while retail shareholder count grew from 18,127 to 31,794 [1].

Our 14-day ATR sits at ₹122.18, or roughly 3.9% of the current share price. Normal daily swings can move the stock ₹100–₹150 without altering the primary trend. Our ₹2,696.82 invalidation stop sits ~3.5 ATRs below CMP and beneath the 30-week SMA (₹2,757.91) [22].

web_blocks.html: Two technical cautions temper the VCP setup. First, relative strength over 28 trading days has lagged (`rs_28d_pct: -20.99%`, `rs_63d_pct: -0.31%`), and the ledger counts 8 distribution days over the last 25 sessions. Second, SEDEMAC is not in the NSE F&O segment (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`). Investors cannot use call spreads or protective puts to cap risk; every share must be managed in cash equity. At the market level, Nifty 50 is in an Uptrend (narrow breadth) with 72.1% of the 61-stock pool above 50-DMA, 3 distribution days, and FIIs net buying +₹5,736.55 Cr vs DIIs selling -₹2,253.58 Cr on November 13, 2026 [21].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Notice how clean the division of labor is between technicals and valuation. The Stage 2 VCP coil tells us NOT to panic-dump all 200 existing shares, because institutional accumulation is holding the 10-week EMA (₹3,116.67). Simultaneously, the 107x trailing P/E tells us NOT to commit fresh cash into the coil. Because SEDEMAC has no listed F&O chain, disciplined cash-equity sizing and hard stop levels are our only risk-control levers.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 was the cold shower of valuation math, Chapter 8 is where we read the footprints of institutional money on the price chart. And here, you and I have to be completely honest about what the tape is showing: SEDEMAC is not breaking down. In fact, on pure technical structure, it is coiling in one of the tightest Stage 2 bases you will see in an Indian mid-cap.

Since listing at ₹1,535 on March 11, 2026, SEDEMAC ran all the way to ₹3,650 before pulling back roughly 14% to Friday's close at ₹3,129.10. Because it only has 167 daily trading bars since its IPO, there is no 200-day simple moving average yet. Instead, we anchor on the 30-week SMA at ₹2,757.91—which is rising steadily beneath price—and the 10-week EMA at ₹3,116.67, where the stock is currently resting.

Look at the compression in volatility and volume. Daily Bollinger bandwidth has narrowed to 7.2%, and the 20-day SMA (₹3,119.50), 50-day SMA (₹3,140.88), and 10-week EMA (₹3,116.67) have converged within a 1% band around ₹3,129. On November 13, only 63,021 shares changed hands—less than half of the 30-day average volume—and the 63-day volume dry-up ratio sits at 0.19. Daily RSI has cooled off to a neutral 49.54. In Mark Minervini and Stan Weinstein terms, sellers have largely dried up inside the ₹2,870–₹3,260 box.

The shareholding pattern explains who has been absorbing supply. Between March 2026 and September 2026, FIIs quadrupled their stake from 2.52% to 10.30%, stepping in as early domestic funds trimmed from 43.93% to 38.34%. Even though the number of retail shareholders rose from 18,127 to 31,794, the total public float share actually declined from 27.31% to 25.12%. Meanwhile, promoters still hold 26.23% with zero shares pledged.

At the same time, a disciplined tape reader never ignores warning signs inside the base. Over the past 25 sessions, the ledger counts 8 distribution days—sessions where institutional selling pushed price down on heavier volume—and 28-day relative strength against the Nifty 50 has slipped to -20.99%. That tells us supply is still being digested near ₹3,250–₹3,500. A decisive breakout requires volume expanding back above 130,000–150,000 shares per day as price clears Pivot R1 at ₹3,509.40.

So why don't we simply buy this VCP breakout? Because technicals tell you *when* a stock is coiled, not *what* it is worth—and a VCP at 107x trailing earnings with 8 recent distribution days and negative 28-day relative strength (-20.99%) carries asymmetric downside if Q3 margins or capex execution disappoint. Furthermore, SEDEMAC is not an NSE F&O stock, so you cannot cap your downside with a cheap call option or collar. If you own it—and we own 200 shares—you manage risk strictly through position sizing and hard cash-equity stop levels.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A tight Stage 2 VCP coil is a wonderful reason *not* to panic-sell an existing winner wholesale, because trend structure remains intact above ₹2,758 (30W SMA). At the same time, a healthy chart never overrides a 107x P/E valuation gate for *new* capital.

book_subsections.title: Key Tape Levels: Support, Breakout Pivot & Hard Invalidation
paragraphs: The immediate support band sits at ₹3,069.92–₹3,175.62, anchored by the 10-week EMA (₹3,116.67) and 20-day SMA (₹3,119.50). Below that lies Pivot S1 at ₹2,869.40 and the rising 30-week SMA at ₹2,757.91. Our hard structural invalidation stop sits at ₹2,696.82—a daily close below ₹2,696.82 would decisively violate the 30-week trend and confirm a Stage 3/4 breakdown.

On the upside, Pivot R1 stands at ₹3,509.40 ahead of the 52-week high at ₹3,650.00. Because `technical_timing_gate` is capped at `CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT` and trailing P/E is 107x, new capital should stand aside regardless of a short-term breakout, while existing holdings use strength toward ₹3,500–₹3,650 to lock in additional gains.

Keep in mind the broader market backdrop as well: Nifty 50 is in a narrow-breadth uptrend with 3 distribution days, and on November 13 FIIs bought +₹5,736.55 Cr while DIIs sold -₹2,253.58 Cr. In narrow markets, high-multiple midcaps can gap down sharply on any earnings miss.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash-Equity Discipline Matters Without an NSE F&O Chain
paragraphs: In large-cap Indian stocks or liquid US equities, an analyst facing a high-multiple Stage 2 VCP can sometimes replace outright equity exposure with a defined-risk bull call spread or protect an existing holding with out-of-the-money puts. On SEDEMAC, our options scan confirms that no listed F&O contract exists—the stock trades strictly in the cash equity segment.

That structural reality makes position sizing and pre-committed stop levels non-negotiable. When you cannot buy convexity through options, your only risk-control lever is share count. If a 107x P/E midcap gaps down 15% on a quarterly margin miss, liquidity in a 63,000-share-per-day tape can thin out rapidly. Right-sizing the holding before a catalyst—and respecting ₹2,696.82 on a daily closing basis—is how you survive single-stock air pockets.

Let us also walk through the exact 4-hour, daily, and weekly moving-average stack so you know what to watch on your own TradingView screen. On the 4-hour chart, EMA20 (₹3,111.64) has crossed just beneath SMA50 (₹3,140.04) with 4H RSI at 51.33, signaling a short-term equilibrium. On the daily chart, 20D SMA (₹3,119.50) and 50D SMA (₹3,140.88) sit within 0.7% of each other, creating a tight price magnet around ₹3,129.10.

On the weekly chart, the 10-week EMA (₹3,116.67) provides immediate dynamic support, while the 30-week SMA (₹2,757.91) defines the primary floor. As long as SEDEMAC holds above ₹2,869.40 (Pivot S1) and ₹2,757.91 (30W SMA), the weekly uptrend remains intact for our trimmed 100-share core position; a close below ₹2,696.82 ends the benefit of the doubt.

Also watch the interplay between FIIs and DIIs in the coming quarters. Foreign institutional investors stepped up from 2.52% to 10.30% between March and September 2026, providing steady institutional sponsorship during post-IPO lock-up expiries. As long as FII ownership holds firm or rises while daily volume expands on up-days above ₹3,300, the base retains institutional backing. However, if distribution days cluster above 10 in a 25-session window or price slices through ₹2,869 on heavy volume, that sponsorship is reversing.

Remember too that SEDEMAC's 14-day ATR is ₹122.18, or roughly 3.9% of the current share price. Normal daily noise can easily swing the stock ₹100 to ₹150 in either direction without changing the primary trend. That is why our hard stop at ₹2,696.82 sits roughly 3.5 ATRs below CMP and cleanly beneath the 30-week SMA (₹2,757.91)—giving the remaining 100 core shares room to breathe while protecting against a genuine Stage 3 breakdown.

Put together, Chapter 8 gives us a clear operational rulebook for the tape: respect the weekly 30W SMA support around ₹2,758 by keeping a trimmed 100-share core stake, but never let a tight volatility squeeze—especially with a flat-to-falling daily 50-DMA and 8 distribution days—tempt you into deploying fresh cash at 107x trailing earnings. Let the 100 remaining shares work for you while the market decides which way this ₹2,870–₹3,509 box resolves.
